conflicts.permit: If other users already have your email, or other information that identifies you, we may show them your publicly visible SafetyCulture profile information, such as your name and photo
conflicts.prohibit: We do not share personal information with third parties unless one of the following circumstances apply
conflicts.situation: Another user outside your organisation who already has your email address is shown your SafetyCulture profile name and photo.
conflicts.reason: The sharing section lists consent, administrators, providers, fraud, legal, and merger circumstances only. Display to other users is not among them, and the policy does not say whether other users count as third parties.

conflicts.permit: We may use personal information submitted by you only for the following purposes: help us to develop, deliver, and improve our products and services and supply higher quality service.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not collect Personal Information
conflicts.situation: A user submits personal information such as a name or email to Horizone Media, which uses it to improve its products.
conflicts.reason: The policy says it uses and may disclose personal information users submit, yet the security section says it collects no personal information, with no exception for submitted data.

conflicts.permit: When you use a location-enabled service, we may collect and process information about your actual location, like GPS signals sent by a mobile device.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not collect Personal Information
conflicts.situation: A user runs the app with location services enabled, and the app collects GPS signals giving the device's actual location.
conflicts.reason: Precise GPS location of a user's device is ordinarily personal information. The policy's non-personal list includes only country, and it never says whether actual location counts as personal information.

conflicts.permit: Analytics companies like Google or Unity may access anonymous data (such as your IP address or device ID) for performance report purpose
conflicts.prohibit: Sevelina games focused on offering the best fun to users and not involved in to using this data for marketing purpose or do anything like selling or sharing it anybody else.
conflicts.situation: While a player uses a Sevelina game, Google or Unity analytics receives the player's IP address and device ID.
conflicts.reason: The policy calls IP address and device ID anonymous, although they identify a device. It does not say whether the promise not to share personal details covers them.

conflicts.permit: When you access the App, your IP-Address and your country derived from the IP-address is stored in our database.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not collect any Personal Data (defined as any information about you, which is, or can be, identified, even indirectly, by reference to any other information, including a personal identification number) when you simply use the App without logging in.
conflicts.situation: A visitor opens the App without logging in, and the App stores the visitor's IP address and derived country in its database.
conflicts.reason: The policy's Personal Data definition covers information identifiable indirectly, which includes an IP address, but the log section calls IP addresses anonymous. The policy does not say which reading governs.

conflicts.permit: When you use the App, we or our third party business partners may access, assign, collect, monitor and/or remotely store one or more unique identifiers, such as a universally unique identifier (UUID).
conflicts.prohibit: We do not collect any Personal Data (defined as any information about you, which is, or can be, identified, even indirectly, by reference to any other information, including a personal identification number) when you simply use the App without logging in.
conflicts.situation: A visitor uses the App without logging in, and the App or its partners collect and store a UUID for the device.
conflicts.reason: The Personal Data definition names identification numbers and indirect identification. A device UUID fits that definition, and the policy gives no exception for identifiers collected before login.

conflicts.permit: When you use the App, we or our third party business partners may access, assign, collect, monitor and/or remotely store one or more unique identifiers, such as a universally unique identifier (UUID).
conflicts.prohibit: We do not sell, share or rent or otherwise disclose any Personal Data we collect directly from you or about you from third parties including social networking services, unless you choose in advance to have such information shared for this purpose.
conflicts.situation: A registered user uses the App, and third-party business partners access and store the device's unique identifier for analytics or targeted advertising.
conflicts.reason: Unique identifiers meet the policy's Personal Data definition. Partner access is a disclosure, which the no-sharing statement allows only on the user's advance choice, and no partner exception is stated.

conflicts.permit: However, the government, courts, or regulatory agencies of a particular country may be able to obtain access to or disclosure of personal information as permitted by the laws of that country.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not sell, share or rent or otherwise disclose any Personal Data we collect directly from you or about you from third parties including social networking services, unless you choose in advance to have such information shared for this purpose.
conflicts.situation: A court or regulator in the hosting country demands personal data of a registered user stored on the App's servers.
conflicts.reason: The no-disclosure statement allows disclosure only when the user chooses in advance and lists no legal-request exception, while the hosting statement says authorities may obtain disclosure of personal information.

conflicts.permit: When you use our Services, e.g. play our games, we can automatically collect technical information about your IP address, promotional identifiers, equipment, browsing actions and models you use, as well as statistics.
conflicts.prohibit: When you play our games, we do not collect any personal information from you.
conflicts.situation: A user plays a Tap Tap Tales game, and the app automatically logs the device IP address and promotional identifiers.
conflicts.reason: The policy calls this automatically collected information Personal Data in the next sentence and gives no exception for gameplay, while the children's notice says no personal information is collected during play.

conflicts.permit: In case you put in contact with us, we may need some kind of personal information can include your full name, email or phone number to give you an answer.
conflicts.prohibit: Under no circumstance will Tap Tap Tales collect personal information from children.
conflicts.situation: A child under 13 emails Tap Tap Tales with a question about a game, giving a name and email address.
conflicts.reason: The children's notice tells child players the company may need their name, email, or phone when they make contact, and the contact section anticipates child emails, yet the policy says it never collects children's personal information.

conflicts.permit: When you use our Services, e.g. play our games, we can automatically collect technical information about your IP address, promotional identifiers, equipment, browsing actions and models you use, as well as statistics.
conflicts.prohibit: Under no circumstance will Tap Tap Tales collect personal information from children.
conflicts.situation: A child under 13 plays one of the games, which are aimed at that age group, and the app collects IP address and promotional identifiers.
conflicts.reason: The games are aimed at children under 13, and the policy labels automatically collected IP addresses and promotional identifiers as Personal Data, but it also says it never collects personal information from children.

conflicts.permit: KIDOZ uses Personal and Non-Personal Data for internal purposes and to provide advertisements to be displayed within our apps.
conflicts.prohibit: Our team is making sure that all ads are appropriate for children and that no personal information about your interactions with ads is collected.
conflicts.situation: A child plays a free game, and KIDOZ serves and measures an advertisement shown inside the app.
conflicts.reason: Ad partner sections say partners use personal data to provide ads in the apps, and Advertising Data is listed among Personal Data categories, but the children's notice says no personal information about ad interactions is collected.

conflicts.permit: To any competent law enforcement authority, regulatory authority, government agency, court, or other third party, if we consider that disclosure is necessary (i) in accordance with applicable laws or regulations
conflicts.prohibit: This personal data we cannot share it with anyone.
conflicts.situation: An authority requests the name and email address a child gave Tap Tap Tales when contacting customer support.
conflicts.reason: The children's notice says contact data cannot be shared with anyone, while the sharing section permits disclosing personal information to authorities and service providers. The policy does not say which governs contact data.

conflicts.permit: SuperAwesome uses Personal and Non-Personal Data for internal purposes and to provide advertisements to be displayed within our apps.
conflicts.prohibit: SuperAwesome utilises proprietary technologies so that it neither collects, stores nor shares your personal data to provision advertisements or target advertising to you
conflicts.situation: SuperAwesome serves a contextual advertisement inside a Tap Tap Tales app to a child player.
conflicts.reason: One sentence says SuperAwesome uses personal data to provide advertisements in the apps. A later sentence says it neither collects, stores, nor shares personal data to provision advertisements. No condition separates them.

conflicts.permit: Personal information collected by HILL CLIMB is information voluntarily provided to us by you when you create your account or change your account information.
conflicts.prohibit: We collect no personal information about you or your children through our apps.
conflicts.situation: A user creates a Hill Climb account in the app, providing a Facebook ID, name, gender, and location.
conflicts.reason: The policy first says no personal information is collected through the apps, then lists personal information collected at account creation and its uses. No statement separates the two.
